reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Verified code at publish_blocks.rs:522-529 publishes all data columns to all 128 subnets without checking network_globals.sampling_subnets. However, this is BY-DESIGN trust boundary differentiation. The flagged code path is the HTTP API block producer endpoint (local validator, operator-controlled, semi-trusted per BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json trust_assumptions.local_validator). Block producers MUST distribute their columns to ALL subnets so all samplers can receive their assigned columns. The 01e property (file: outputs/01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json, line 914-929, invariant: 'Publishing data columns must only occur on subnets the node is subscribed to (custody/sampling)') and subgraph SG-010 'distributed_blob_publishing' apply to GOSSIP RE-PUBLISHING (receive block from gossip, query EL, convert, re-publish), NOT to initial block producer publication via HTTP API. The subgraph entry point is 'receive valid beacon_block...from gossip' (line 6), confirming this is about re-publishing, not producer publishing. Different trust levels for local validator API vs P2P gossip are intentional architectural design. The custody subnet restriction prevents gossip pollution from re-publishing, but block producers need unrestricted publishing to bootstrap column distribution across the network.
